name: Nevada
nameStory: Nevada is Spanish for 'snow-covered,' which is a joke on the driest state in America. It is named for the Sierra Nevada on its western edge - and those mountains are exactly why Nevada is dry, because they wring the rain out of Pacific storms before anything reaches the far side. The name explains the desert.
capitalStory: Carson City, named for the scout Kit Carson, exploded in the 1860s because the Comstock Lode - the richest silver strike in American history - was in the hills right next door. The silver is why the state is nicknamed Silver State, and why it became a state at all.

majorFeatures.name: Great Basin
majorFeatures.note: Water here never reaches the sea

majorFeatures.name: Lake Tahoe
majorFeatures.note: Deep alpine lake shared with California

majorFeatures.name: Mojave Desert
majorFeatures.note: The hot southern corner around Las Vegas

majorFeatures.name: Lake Mead
majorFeatures.note: Colorado River reservoir behind Hoover Dam

funFacts: Nevada is the driest state, averaging about 10 inches of precipitation a year.
It has more separate mountain ranges than any other state - over 300 of them, running in parallel north-south stripes.
In the Great Basin, rivers just end: they evaporate or sink, and none of that water ever reaches an ocean.
About 80% of Nevada is owned by the federal government, more than any other state.
whyItMatters: Nevada was rushed into the Union in 1864, well short of the usual population requirement, because Lincoln needed the electoral votes and Senate support for the 13th Amendment. Its flag still reads 'Battle Born.'
